Grammar extra
The perfect infinitive
See page 158.
Use the perfect infinitive for events in a period of time that lead up to the present or to a point in the past.
You can use the perfect infinitive after verbs like seem, appear, and happen
He seems to have had a lot of respect for older people
You can use the perfect infinitive after verbs such as acknowledge, believe, consider, know, say, and think
Sheis considered to have formed some extremely effective political alliances
You can use the perfect infinitive after would like/ love/hate, etc., for events that did not happen.
I'd love to have met Leonardo da Vinci.
In conversation
Li-yun would like to have spoken face-to-face with Confucius

to do it, not I would like to have done it. Some
